title: A Retrospective Study Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Prefabricated Functional Orthodontic Appliance in the Rehabilitation of Atypical Deglutition: An Ultrasound Approach
content: Objective: To assess the impact of a Prefabricated Functional Orthodontic Appliance (PFOA), used in conjunction with Myofunctional Therapy (MT), on atypical deglutition in children, using ultrasound (US)and functional parameters. Methods: A single-centre, single-operator retrospective study involving 59 children with atypical deglutition associated with Class II malocclusion. Two groups were compared: MT alone (n = 27) and MT combined with a PFOA (n = 32). The primary criterion was the variation in hyoid–mandibular distance (HMD) between rest and deglutition (HMD rest – HMD deglutition). Secondary criteria included tongue kinetics, resting tongue position, compensatory facial contractions, breathing, sleep quality, compliance and several exploratory postural analyses. The primary monitoring period was 2 months, with a subgroup undergoing extended monitoring. Results: The primary criteria improved significantly in both groups (p < 0.001). No significant differences between the groups were observed at 2 months, but the sensitivity analysis showed a favourable trend in the MT + PFOA group. Several secondary criteria improved significantly in both groups, with more marked positive trends clinically speaking in the MT + PFOA group, particularly for tongue movement, tongue posture, lip control, breathing and sleep disorders. The lack of statistical significance for some of these criteria appears to be mainly due to the small sample size and the very short monitoring period (2 months), whereas PFOAs are usually used over periods of at least 6 months. Conclusion: The addition of PFOA to MT does not provide statistically significant superiority over hyoid elevation at 2 months, but is associated with favourable functional trends consistent with the expected role of PFOA as an adjunctive therapy. A prospective, randomised study involving a larger sample size and a monitoring period of at least 6 months is required to confirm these results.
